findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: hiring_posts, company_lookup, networking_plan, get_my_account, best_matches, get_application, undo_change, get_inbox, mark_messages_read, get_unread, whats_new, get_email_preferences, update_email_preferences, get_hiring_overview, post_job, update_post, close_post, reject_applicant, message_applicant, get_hiring_inbox, mark_hiring_messages_read, get_screening_autopilot, set_screening_autopilot, get_hiring_updates, search_candidates, request_introduction · Private data: company_lookup, find_people, connection_score, us_visa_salaries, get_profile, upload_cv, confirm_note, move_on_tracker, log_outside_application, apply, list_contacts, add_contact, draft_outreach, list_actions, get_applicant · Public sink: hiring_posts, employer_reply_rate, referral_note, interview_practice, update_profile, upload_cv, update_preferences, best_matches, edit_application, apply, list_escalations, get_usage, get_email_preferences, update_email_preferences, post_job, update_post, close_post, message_applicant, search_candidates, request_introduction · Destructive: get_about_me, delete_note.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
